title: Redrawing the Map in New York

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报 Dealbook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 Dealbook 峰会的现场，采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的一些领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、佐兰·莫达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你们可以实时观看其中一些毫无保留、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并免费阅读我们所有的新闻报道一个月。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望大家锁定收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你们一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is a daily.
sentences.zh: 这是一档日常播客。

sentences.en: Over the past decade,
sentences.zh: 在过去十年里，

sentences.en: Republicans have successfully redrawn congressional districts across the country to their political advantage.
sentences.zh: 共和党人成功地在全国范围内重新划分了国会选区，以获取政治优势。

sentences.en: Now, Democrats in New York say it's time to use the same playbook.
sentences.zh: 现在，纽约的民主党人表示，是时候使用同样的战术了。

sentences.en: Astead Herndon spoke with our colleague, Nick Fandos, Thursday, September 23rd.
sentences.zh: 阿斯特德·赫恩顿于9月23日星期四采访了我们的同事尼克·范多斯。

sentences.en: So, Nick, you're in New York now.
sentences.zh: 那么，尼克，你现在在纽约。

sentences.en: Was there not enough good breakfast sandwiches in Washington,
sentences.zh: 华盛顿难道没有足够好吃的早餐三明治

sentences.en: D.C.
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚特区

sentences.en: for your liking?
sentences.zh: 来合你的胃口吗？

sentences.en: That bagel scene couldn't keep up.
sentences.zh: 那里的贝果风潮已经跟不上节奏了。

sentences.en: That's why I decided I needed to start looking a little further afield.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我决定开始把目光投向更远的地方。

sentences.en: So, you traded locales, but the fight in Washington was about, you know, things like voting rights and gerrymandering.
sentences.zh: 所以，你换了地方，但华盛顿争论的焦点，你知道的，是诸如投票权和划定有利选区之类的事情。

sentences.en: That seems to be what's happening in New York also.
sentences.zh: 纽约似乎也正在发生同样的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's funny.
sentences.zh: 对，这挺有意思的。

sentences.en: I mean, literally, I spent a lot of my spring and summer really focused on Democrats pushing Congress to try and pass this major voting rights legislation.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，实际上，我的很多春夏季节都真正专注于推动国会通过这项重大的投票权立法。

sentences.en: Which also included a big provision that would have outlawed gerrymandering of congressional districts across the country.
sentences.zh: 其中还包括一项重要条款，本该取缔全国各地国会选区的选区操纵。

sentences.en: And lo and behold, I get up here to New York to start my new job.
sentences.zh: 而结果呢，我来到纽约开始新工作，

sentences.en: And that's the first story that smacks me right in the face.
sentences.zh: 这成了迎面砸向我的第一个新闻。

sentences.en: I mean, New York, it turns out, is in the thick of it and is going to be a very big part of the national story on gerrymandering and elections in this coming year.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，事实证明，纽约正处于风口浪尖，并且将在今年关于选区操纵和选举的全国新闻中占据很大一部分。

sentences.en: What is happening in New York specifically related to gerrymandering?
sentences.zh: 纽约具体发生了什么与选区操纵相关的事情？

sentences.en: So, this year, New York, like every other state in the country, got back detailed population data from the 2020 census.
sentences.zh: 所以，今年纽约和全国其他所有州一样，从2020年人口普查中获得了详细的人口数据。

sentences.en: And the Constitution says that once this data is in hand showing where people have moved and populations have increased and declined, every state has to go and redraw its
sentences.zh: 宪法规定，一旦掌握了这些显示人们迁移地点以及人口增长和下降的数据，每个州都必须重新划分其

sentences.en: congressional and legislative districts.
sentences.zh: 国会和地方立法选区。

sentences.en: And so, where you lay the lines could go a long way in determining who's going to control the House of Representatives in D.C.
sentences.zh: 因此，你如何划定这些边界，对于决定谁将控制华盛顿的众议院有着深远的影响。

sentences.en: Right now, that's the
sentences.zh: 目前，控制众议院的是

sentences.en: Democrats by only the slimmest of margins.
sentences.zh: 民主党，而且优势极其微弱。

sentences.en: And Republicans think they have a good shot in the
sentences.zh: 共和党人认为他们在

sentences.en: 2022 midterms to retake control of the House.
sentences.zh: 2022年中期选举中有很大机会重新夺回众议院的控制权。

sentences.en: And the redistricting process could really either help them do that or make it harder for them to do that, depending on who gets the upper hand.
sentences.zh: 而选区重划的过程确实要么能帮他们做到这一点，要么会增加他们的难度，这取决于谁占据上风。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, coming out of the census, state legislatures are empowered to draw these new maps.
sentences.zh: 因此，根据人口普查结果，州议会被授权绘制这些新地图。

sentences.en: And those maps will develop the sort of rules of the game when we think about the midterms next year.
sentences.zh: 而这些地图将为我们思考明年的中期选举奠定某种游戏规则。

sentences.en: But that's happening all across the country and states.
sentences.zh: 但这在全国各州都在发生。

sentences.en: What specifically is different here about New York?
sentences.zh: 纽约这里究竟有什么不同？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, there's a couple of things I think that are really interesting about New York and will tell us something about this whole process.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为纽约有几点非常有趣，它们将向我们揭示整个过程的一些情况。

sentences.en: One, just as a baseline, New York is a really big state, right?
sentences.zh: 首先，作为一个基准，纽约是一个非常大的州，对吧？

sentences.en: So, it's one of the largest single delegations to Congress in the country, up there with Texas and California and Florida.
sentences.zh: 因此，它是全国向国会派遣单一代表团人数最多的州之一，与得克萨斯州、加利福尼亚州和佛罗里达州并列。

sentences.en: So, you're just talking about a lot of seats right off the bat.
sentences.zh: 所以，从一开始这就是一个庞大的席位数量。

sentences.en: But something happened in New York or was supposed to have changed after the last time this redistricting process played out in 2010 to 2012.
sentences.zh: 但纽约发生了一些事情，或者说在2010年至2012年上次选区重划进程结束后，本来应该有所改变。

sentences.en: Back then, lawmakers here who had a divided
sentences.zh: 当时，这里的议员们面临着分裂的

sentences.en: Republican and Democratic government really struggled to draw lines.
sentences.zh: 共和与民主两党政府，在划定边界时遇到了很大困难。

sentences.en: It was like a total mess.
sentences.zh: 那简直是一团糟。

sentences.en: They couldn't come to an agreement and ultimately had to ask courts to get involved.
sentences.zh: 他们无法达成一致，最终不得不请法院介入。

sentences.en: And they appointed a special master and drew lines that nobody really loved, but they could live with.
sentences.zh: 他们任命了一名特别主审官，并划定了没有人真正喜欢、但勉强能接受的边界。

sentences.en: But as a part of this whole partisan fight, there was an agreement to put together for the first time
sentences.zh: 但作为这场党派斗争的一部分，各方达成了一项协议，首次组建

sentences.en: a commission that would be bipartisan and try to take the process of drawing district lines out of
sentences.zh: 一个两党委员会，试图将划定选区边界的工作从

sentences.en: the hands of politicians and give it to a more independent group of people who would have to find a bipartisan solution.
sentences.zh: 政客手中剥离出来，交给一个更独立的群体，由他们去寻找两党都能接受的解决方案。

sentences.en: And so, they put it before voters as a constitutional amendment.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们将此作为一项宪法修正案提交给选民。

sentences.en: And in 2014, that was adopted by a wide margin.
sentences.zh: 在2014年，该修正案以巨大优势获得通过。

sentences.en: And what it meant is that this year, 2021, this redistricting cycle is supposed to be the first time that this independent commission takes over and draws fair
sentences.zh: 这意味着今年，即2021年，这一选区重划周期本应是这个独立委员会第一次接管并划定

sentences.en: maps down the middle that just represented the state as it was and didn't tip towards the Republicans or the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 公正居中的地图，这些地图只是反映了该州的原貌，既不偏向共和党，也不偏向民主党。

sentences.en: So, the idea was that instead of Republican and Democratic lawmakers having some political fight about these maps, that this bipartisan commission would come to an independent,
sentences.zh: 所以，当时的设想是，与其让共和党和民主党议员为这些地图展开政治斗争，不如让这个两党委员会对地图做出独立的、

sentences.en: politically neutral decision about the maps that would be fair.
sentences.zh: 政治中立且公正的决定。

sentences.en: Yeah, that was the idea and the ambition.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是当时的构想和宏伟目标。

sentences.en: But in the time between when New York voters went to the polls and approved this commission created in 2014, and now voters also went and gave Democrats
sentences.zh: 但在纽约选民投票批准建立这个2014年委员会的这段时间里，选民们还在奥尔巴尼的立法机构中赋予了民主党

sentences.en: super majorities in the legislature in Albany and kept the governor's mansion under Democratic control.
sentences.zh: 超级多数席位，并使州长府邸继续由民主党掌控。

sentences.en: So, basically, now you have Democrats in control of everything, and so convincingly so, that they can constitutionally come in and just overpower the independent commission.
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上，现在民主党人控制了一切，而且优势如此压倒性，以至于他们可以在宪法框架内直接介入并压制这个独立委员会。

sentences.en: You are speaking to my political nerd soul, but I want to slow it down.
sentences.zh: 你简直说到了我这个政治迷的心坎里，但我想放慢节奏。

sentences.en: You're saying that Democrats have a large enough majority in both the state assembly and the state senate that they
sentences.zh: 你是说，民主党在州议会和州参议院都拥有足够大的多数席位，以至于他们

sentences.en: can actually override anything that this independent bipartisan commission comes up with when it comes to redistricting.
sentences.zh: 在选区重划方面，实际上可以推翻这个独立的两党委员会提出的任何方案。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: So, that commission can go and do its work and hold dozens of hearings, and it could produce sterling maps.
sentences.zh: 所以，那个委员会可以去开展工作并举行数十场听证会，还能制作出色的地图。

sentences.en: And, you know, if top Democrats in Albany or in Washington decided we don't like it, they can just tear it up and throw it out, as long as all their members go along with them.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，如果奥尔巴尼或华盛顿的高层民主党人决定不喜欢它，他们大可以直接撕毁并扔掉它，只要他们的所有成员都投赞成票。

sentences.en: They, at the end of the day, end up with the pen and the map.
sentences.zh: 说到底，他们手里握着笔和地图。

sentences.en: And, you know, there are some rules that govern how they proceed from there, but they basically can draw lines where they want.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，有一些规则管辖着他们接下来如何行事，但他们基本上可以在自己想要的地方划线。

sentences.en: And there's an opportunity here, I think, that folks in Washington and Albany are beginning to see for them to really try and run the table and squeeze out a lot of Republicans.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，华盛顿和奥尔巴尼的人们开始看到一个机会，让他们能够真正尝试掌控全局并排挤掉许多共和党人。

sentences.en: So, with increased Democratic control of this process, can you tell me what that actually looks like?
sentences.zh: 那么，随着民主党对这一过程控制力的增强，你能告诉我这实际上是什么样子的吗？

sentences.en: What can Democrats do with this newfound power in relationship to these maps?
sentences.zh: 民主党人如何利用这股新获得的权力来处理这些地图？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, if you kind of picture a map of New York State in front of yourself, Estad, you know, there's kind of three or four big regions.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你脑海中浮现出一张纽约州地图，阿斯特德，你知道，大概有三四个大区域。

sentences.en: And basically, in every one of those regions, in Long Island, in New York City, and upstate, there are Republican seats that are currently held
sentences.zh: 基本上，在每一个区域，在长岛、纽约市和北部地区，都有目前由

sentences.en: by Republican members of Congress that Democrats could move more liberal voters into, basically, and turn blue.
sentences.zh: 共和党国会议员占据的共和党席位，民主党基本上可以把更多自由派选民移入这些选区，从而将其变成蓝色。

sentences.en: So, if you take all of that as a whole, and you consider the fact that New York also is going to lose one congressional seat overall, because it didn't keep pace with growth
sentences.zh: 所以，如果把所有这些作为一个整体来看，并考虑到纽约由于人口增长没有跟上

sentences.en: in the rest of the country, what you could end up with is a scenario that would be something like
sentences.zh: 全国其他地区的速度，总体上将失去一个国会席位，你最终可能会得到一个类似于这样的方案：

sentences.en: 23 Democrats and only three Republicans representing the state of New York and Washington, compared to 19 Democrats and eight Republicans today.
sentences.zh: 23名民主党人和只有3名共和党人代表纽约州前往华盛顿，而今天是19名民主党人和8名共和党人。

sentences.en: That's a pretty significant swing.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当大的摇摆幅度。

sentences.en: I mean, as many as five Republicans that could be losing their seats after next year's midterMs.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，多达五名共和党人可能会在明年的中期选举后失去席位。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Now, of course, candidates have to run and win, and flukes can always happen.
sentences.zh: 当然，候选人必须参选并获胜，意外总是会发生。

sentences.en: Maybe they'll lose a winnable seat.
sentences.zh: 也许他们会输掉一个本可赢下的席位。

sentences.en: But the conditions will be pretty favorable for them to get the result they want.
sentences.zh: 但客观条件对他们取得想要的结果相当有利。

sentences.en: Isn't this a bit ironic?
sentences.zh: 这难道不有点讽刺吗？

sentences.en: I hear Democrats so often, particularly in Washington, talk about the need to eliminate gerrymandering, as you mentioned, pushing that bill in D.C.
sentences.zh: 我经常听到民主党人，特别是在华盛顿，谈论消除选区操纵的必要性，正如你所提到的，他们在华盛顿特区推动的那项法案

sentences.en: that would stop states from doing it.
sentences.zh: 将阻止各州这样做。

sentences.en: So, you're saying that even as they're doing that in D.C.,
sentences.zh: 所以你是说，即便他们在华盛顿特区这样做，

sentences.en: Democrats on the state level are engaging in that same thing.
sentences.zh: 地方层面的民主党人却在从事同样的事情。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And that's one of the things that makes this so fascinating to watch.
sentences.zh: 这就是让这件事如此引人注目的原因之一。

sentences.en: Remember, you know, New York's senior senator, whose seat is not at stake here, but is involved in this process,
sentences.zh: 记住，你知道，纽约的资深参议员——他的席位在这里没有受到威胁，但也参与了这个过程——

sentences.en: is Chuck Schumer, who's the majority leader of the Senate, who's leading the push for that bill that I spent so much time covering in my old job.
sentences.zh: 是查克·舒默，他是参议院多数党领袖，正是他在带头推动我过去在工作中花大量时间报道的那项法案。

sentences.en: And, you know, the same day that this process was getting underway in New York, Schumer was down in D.C.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，就在这个进程在纽约展开的同一天，舒默正在华盛顿特区

sentences.en: Partisans across the country are sharpening their knives for a coming spade of vicious gerrymandering, which further threatens to divide our politics.
sentences.zh: 全国各地的党派人士都在磨刀霍霍，准备迎接即将到来的一轮恶毒的选区操纵，这进一步威胁到我们的政治分裂。

sentences.en: Talking about how horrible gerrymandering is and how we need to get rid of it on the national level.
sentences.zh: 谈论选区操纵是多么可怕，以及我们需要在国家层面消除它。

sentences.en: And so you have this real kind of dissonance between Democrats' stated values and what they're doing in states like New York and some others across the country.
sentences.zh: 所以，民主党人宣称的价值观与他们在纽约以及全国其他一些州所作所为之间，存在着一种真正的割裂。

sentences.en: This is unacceptable.
sentences.zh: 这是不可接受的。

sentences.en: So the Senate must act.
sentences.zh: 所以参议院必须采取行动。

sentences.en: I yield the floor.
sentences.zh: 我发言完毕。

sentences.en: But, you know, when I talk to Democrats, they are perfectly aware of this hypocrisy and basically
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，当我与民主党人交谈时，他们对这种伪善心知肚明，并且基本上

sentences.en: say they're willing to live with it because they don't want their values to get in the way of what they see is at stake here.
sentences.zh: 表示他们愿意接受这一点，因为他们不想让自己的价值观阻碍他们眼中真正重要的利益。

sentences.en: And we've got to remember, it's huge.
sentences.zh: 我们必须记住，这事关重大。

sentences.en: The 2022 midterms will determine who is in control of Congress.
sentences.zh: 2022年中期选举将决定谁控制国会。

sentences.en: And gerrymandering, laying down kind of the lines on the playing field, is going to go a long way in determining that outcome.
sentences.zh: 而选区操纵，即划定竞技场的边界，将在很大程度上决定这一结果。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费探索《时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.

sentences.en: So Nick, how does what's happening in New York fit into the national picture and the midterm elections, which are, you know, somewhat shockingly, only about a year away?

sentences.en: But as we were just alluding to,
sentences.zh: 但正如我们刚刚提到的，

sentences.en: So basically, they've got to come up with some sort of compromise or agreement to move forward.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，他们必须达成某种妥协或协议才能继续推进。

sentences.en: And the lines are probably going to end up being fairer as a result.
sentences.zh: 因此，最终划出的边界可能更公平。

sentences.en: Then there are states that truly have independent commissions that can't be overwritten by politicians in the legislature.

sentences.en: You know, there are Republican and Democratic states that fall into this category.

sentences.en: Okay.

sentences.en: And it's been a proud or perhaps embarrassing political tradition in this country ever since.

sentences.en: But, you know, I think what I take away from this cycle, and if you look at the past several, states are getting more and more

sentences.en: Democrats wanted to end the protection, but Republicans refused.
sentences.zh: 民主党人希望结束这种保护，但共和党人拒绝了。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Sidney Harper and Austin Mitchell, with help from Soraya Shockley and Rob Zipko.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由西德尼·哈珀（Sidney Harper）和奥斯汀·米切尔（Austin Mitchell）制作，索赖亚·肖克利（Soraya Shockley）和罗布·齐普科（Rob Zipko）提供了帮助。

sentences.en: It was edited by M.J.
sentences.zh: 节目由M.J.

sentences.en: Davis-Lynn and Dave Shaw.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯-林恩（Davis-Lynn）和戴夫·肖（Dave Shaw）剪辑。

sentences.en: Original music by Marion Lozano.
sentences.zh: 原创音乐由马里昂·洛萨诺（Marion Lozano）创作。

sentences.en: And engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 音频工程由克里斯·伍德（Chris Wood）负责。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landfork of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题曲由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格（Jim Brunberg）和本·兰德福克（Ben Landfork）创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗（Michael Barbaro）。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》中，我们正在为假期招待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要完全黑暗才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们会不会失去意识才能睡着。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是指，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的要求。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症、食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶的人？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在纽约时报应用程序或您喜欢收听的任何地方查找《Wirecutter秀》。
